What Water Heater Service Involves

Water heater service covers everything from routine repairs to full system replacement. When a unit is not heating properly, a licensed technician diagnoses the cause, gas or electric, tank or tankless, sediment buildup or a failed part, and explains the repair before starting. When a unit needs to be replaced, the same visit becomes a chance to size the new system correctly, so it matches your household’s hot water demand instead of running short or wasting energy. Russell’s American Mechanical services both major types of water heaters:

  • Tank Water Heaters: Traditional systems that store and heat a set volume of water, repaired or replaced to match your household’s needs.
  • Tankless Water Heaters: On-demand tankless systems that heat water as you use it, installed for households that want more space and a longer-lasting system.
  • Repair and Inspection: Diagnosing issues like inconsistent temperature, leaks, or unusual noises, then fixing the specific problem.
  • Installation and Replacement: Sizing and installing a new system, tank or tankless, when repair is no longer the better option, including any gas line work a new unit needs.

Signs You Need Water Heater Repair or Replacement

Most tank water heaters last 8 to 12 years, and tankless systems often last longer with proper maintenance. As a water heater nears the end of that range, repairs become more frequent and less cost-effective, so age is the first thing worth checking when something goes wrong. Rising energy bills, rusty or discolored water, and inconsistent water temperature are signs the unit is struggling, even if it has not failed completely yet. If a repair costs close to a third of what a new installation would run, or if the unit is already past its expected lifespan, replacement is usually the better long-term value, and financing options can spread that cost when the timing is not ideal. A technician can inspect the unit, walk you through both options, and quote each one so you can compare before deciding.

FAQs

How can I make my water heater last longer?

Schedule annual maintenance to flush sediment from the tank and inspect for leaks or rust. Keep the thermostat set to 120 degrees F to reduce wear on internal parts, since a tank water heater typically lasts 8 to 12 years with regular care. Addressing small issues, like a failing anode rod or a slow leak, before they become bigger problems is one of the most effective ways to extend that lifespan.

What's the number one mistake homeowners make with water heaters?

The most common mistake is skipping routine maintenance, letting sediment build up in the tank until it reduces efficiency and shortens the unit’s life. An annual flush and inspection catches this early and is far less expensive than an emergency repair or early replacement.

What are the signs a water heater requires repairs?

Watch for inconsistent water temperature, rumbling or popping noises from the tank, discolored or rusty water, and any moisture or leaking around the base of the unit. A pilot light that will not stay lit is another common sign on gas models. Catching these early usually means a simpler repair instead of a full replacement.

How long does a water heater installation take?

Most standard water heater installations finish in a single visit. Switching from a tank system to tankless, or making electrical or gas line changes, can add time, and your technician will give you a specific estimate before work begins.

Should I choose a tank or tankless water heater?

Tank water heaters usually cost less upfront and work well for most households. Tankless systems cost more initially but heat water on demand, take up less space, and typically last longer. Our technicians can walk you through both options based on your household’s hot water use and your budget.

How much does water heater repair or replacement cost?

Cost depends on the type of unit, the extent of the problem, and whether you choose repair or full replacement. Russell’s American Mechanical provides an upfront quote before any work begins, so repair and replacement can be compared on real numbers.
